chapter_title: Concerning the Five Saviours, the Resurrectors of
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Five Powers of Regeneration

**¶2:** [GAP-1: the spiritual sense requires here an identification of the first power of regeneration or its operation] its operation within [GAP-2: the spiritual sense requires here a description of what this first awakening accomplishes within the soul].

**¶3:** The second power of spiritual awakening is [GAP-3: the spiritual sense requires here a second distinct divine operation or faculty through which regeneration proceeds — likely an intermediary influx between the inmost divine and the illumined understanding].

**¶4:** And the third power of spiritual awakening is the Divine Love itself, the Originating [GAP-4: the spiritual sense requires here a qualifier of the Divine as source or origin of all derivative good], because by Divine Truth proceeding from that Love shall all interior affections that constitute spiritual life [GAP-5: the spiritual sense requires here a verb of awakening, liberation, or vivification] gather inward and return toward conjunction with the Divine, and they receive [GAP-6: the spiritual sense requires here the specific quality bestowed — fullness, blessedness, or eternal life] and enter the state of heavenly peace.

**¶5:** The fourth power of spiritual awakening is the Divine Wisdom operating within the understanding, because [GAP-7: the spiritual sense requires here a description of how interior illumination raises the rational mind from falsity into perception of truth].

**¶6:** The fifth power of spiritual awakening toward those in states of genuine good [GAP-8: the spiritual sense requires here a qualifier — those in charity, the regenerated, or the elect affections] is the Divine Love in its foundational and sustaining aspect [GAP-9: the spiritual sense requires here how this grounding divine principle was established from eternity or within the order of regeneration]. [GAP-10: The spiritual sense requires here that the Divine] pervades all faculties of will and understanding, and remains immovable in constancy [GAP-11: the spiritual sense requires here a description of the permanence or universality of this divine presence]. The Divine shall remove the veils of natural appearance from [GAP-12: the spiritual sense requires here what is unveiled — interior truths, or the glorified divine form] over those faculties [GAP-13: the spiritual sense requires here the condition or manner of this unveiling], and draws all regenerated affections toward conjunction with itself [GAP-14: the spiritual sense requires here the means or quality of this drawing — through love, through delight, through interior perception], according to the Divine Providence [GAP-15: the spiritual sense requires here how the divine will operates — freely, without compulsion, in mercy], and [GAP-16: the spiritual sense requires here a verb — vivifies, purifies, perfects, or conjoins] them, and raises them into established spiritual life [GAP-17: the spiritual sense requires here the state or place of this establishment — in heavenly order, in the celestial degree], and they remain in that conjunction until [GAP-18: the spiritual sense requires here the final consummation — the completion of all regeneration, the last separation of good from evil, or the full restitution of all interiorly living things to the Divine].

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: [The first resurrector is the Living Spirit, who awakens] it therein [and raises it up].
The second resurrector is [the Mother of Life].
And the third resurrector is the Father, the First [Man], because by his word shall all lives [arise and] gather in and go to him, and they receive [life] and rest.
The fourth resurrector is the Light Mind, because [it awakens the soul from forgetfulness].

The fifth resurrector to the good [souls] is the Father, the First established one [from the beginning]. [He encompasses] all the powers, and he stands firm [over all things]. He shall unveil the [image] over them [in that day], and he draws them to him [by his love], his will [and his mercy], and he [purifies] them, and he stands them up [in his light] there, and they remain until [the end of all things].

fills.fill: The first resurrector is the Living Spirit, who awakens
fills.explanation: The Living Spirit is the first cosmic redeemer in Manichaean soteriology who initiates the process of light-redemption, corresponding to the Lord's initial preservation of remains; the verb "awakens" fits the resurrection theme and governs the surviving "it therein."
The first resurrector's action of awakening the light within must culminate in raising it, completing the resurrection motif that defines the chapter's theme.

The Mother of Life is the principal intermediary between the Father of Greatness and the lower emanations in Manichaean cosmology, matching the spiritual reading's requirement for an intermediary influx between the inmost divine and the illumined understanding.

The First Man (Ohrmizd/Nāšā Qadmāyā) is a standard Manichaean divine title distinguishing this Father-figure from the Fifth resurrector; it corresponds to the Divine Human as the originating form of all derivative good in Swedenborg.

In a chapter on resurrection, the verb 'arise' naturally precedes 'gather in and go to him,' completing a three-fold sequence of awakening, ingathering, and return that matches the spiritual sense of vivification and liberation.

In the Kephalaia, the redeemed receive 'life' upon returning to the divine; this corresponds to the spiritual sense of receiving eternal life or blessedness, paired naturally with 'rest' as the twofold gift of redemption.

fills.fill: it awakens the soul from forgetfulness
fills.explanation: The Light Mind's defining function in Manichaean soteriology is awakening the soul from forgetfulness (the sleep of ignorance); this corresponds to Swedenborg's description of Divine Wisdom raising the rational mind from falsity into perception of truth.
The 'good souls' is natural Kephalaia phrasing for those who have received the light and are in states of genuine good, corresponding to the regenerated or those in charity in the spiritual sense.

The Father as 'the First established one from the beginning' expresses the eternal grounding of the divine principle prior to all emanation, matching the spiritual sense of being established from eternity.
The Father of Greatness 'encompasses all the powers' expresses the divine pervading of all faculties, a standard Kephalaia description of the supreme deity's universal presence.
Standing firm 'over all things' expresses the universality and permanence of the divine presence, complementing the encompassing of all powers with authoritative immovability over all creation.

The divine 'image' (eikon) is the standard Kephalaia term for the glorified divine form that is revealed to the redeemed, corresponding to Swedenborg's unveiling of the Divine Human form to the regenerated understanding.
The eschatological temporal marker 'in that day' is a standard Kephalaia phrase describing the condition and time of the final unveiling, when the divine image is revealed over the redeemed.
The divine drawing operates through love, corresponding to Swedenborg's teaching that the Lord draws all things to Himself through the attraction of Divine Love rather than compulsion.

The divine will operating through mercy corresponds to the spiritual reading's emphasis on the divine operating freely and without compulsion; 'mercy' is a standard divine attribute in the Kephalaia paired with will.

Purification is the essential intermediate step between being drawn to the Divine and being established in spiritual life; it corresponds to the Manichaean process of separating light from dark mixture and Swedenborg's purification of the natural mind.

Being 'stood up in his light' expresses establishment in the celestial degree or heavenly order, using the Kephalaia's primary term for the divine realm where the redeemed are permanently established.

The final consummation when all light is separated from darkness and restored to the Divine corresponds to the last separation of good from evil in Swedenborg; 'the end of all things' is a standard Kephalaia eschatological phrase.
